protocol: Subject-wise protocol differs from the paper; test < 10 subjects per fold (20 total)

scenes.title: Sleep staging from one EEG channel
scenes.lead:
A stage for every
30 seconds of sleep
body: Five labels describe wakefulness and sleep.
This study uses a compact CNN + BiGRU.
The original SST / contrastive pipeline is a different model.
captions: Sleep staging assigns a label to each 30-second EEG epoch across a recorded night.
We present a simpler CNN + BiGRU study, not a replication of the original paper.
scenes.note: Conceptual EEG scene. The trace is illustrative, not a recorded signal.

scenes.title: The evaluated cohort
body: 42,307 retained EEG epochs
Sleep-EDF Expanded, single-channel EEG
All headline results use the same evaluated cohort.
captions: The evaluated subset contains 20 participants and 39 nights, with 42,307 retained epochs.
Participant separation matters because different nights from the same person are related.
scenes.note: Each figure represents one participant. Counts come from the archived closeout.

scenes.title: Five sleep-stage labels
scenes.lead:
W, N1, N2, N3
and REM
body: W means wakefulness. N1 is light sleep.
N2 and N3 are deeper non-REM stages.
REM is rapid eye movement sleep.
captions: The model predicts one of five labels. We evaluate every class, not only overall accuracy.
Macro-F1 gives each class equal weight. Accuracy counts all correctly classified epochs.
scenes.note: Stage colors identify categories. The animated timeline is illustrative.

scenes.title: Subject-wise evaluation
body: Ten folds rotate the held-out participants.
Each person appears in test exactly once.
Validation chooses checkpoints, not test.
captions: Each fold separates participants into training, validation and test sets without subject overlap.
Only two participants form each test fold. Small fold samples create substantial variability.
scenes.note: Subject-wise protocol differs from the paper; test < 10 subjects per fold (20 total)

chapters.title: How the model reads a night

scenes.title: EEG becomes a time-frequency image
body: Channel: EEG Fpz-Cz at 100 Hz
STFT separates frequency content over time.
Log-spectrograms feed the CNN.
captions: The short-time Fourier transform describes how frequency content changes within each EEG epoch.
The resulting log-spectrogram has 129 frequency bins and 29 time bins.
scenes.note: The example trace and spectrogram illustrate the transform. They are not measured data.

scenes.title: The CNN encodes each epoch
body: Three convolution blocks: 32, 64, 128 channels
BatchNorm, ReLU and pooling in each block
A 128-dimensional embedding represents one epoch.
captions: The CNN extracts local time-frequency patterns and compresses each epoch into a feature vector.
These are conceptual feature blocks. Their colors do not represent learned activations.
scenes.note: Architecture from src/model.py. Feature maps and filters are conceptual.

scenes.title: BiGRU adds within-night context
body: Two GRU layers, 128 hidden units per direction
Forward and backward context yield 256 features.
The classifier outputs five logits per epoch.
captions: A bidirectional GRU reads the sequence in both directions and combines neighboring context.
Sequences stay within a single night. Bidirectional context makes this an offline model.
scenes.note: Illustrative sequence. Connections show architecture, not estimated causal effects.

scenes.title: One inference path for validation and test
body: Inference stride: 5 EEG epochs
Overlapping windows cover the recorded night.
The model averages logits before selecting a label.
captions: Validation and test use the same sliding-window inference path with stride five.
Evaluation mode disables dropout and uses saved BatchNorm statistics. Windows never cross nights.
scenes.note: Window placement is illustrative. The stride and averaging rule come from the code.

scenes.title: The baseline failed on specific nights
scenes.lead:
Some predictions
collapsed to one class
body: SC4142: 19.01% accuracy, all predictions W
SC4062: 18.60% accuracy
SC4021: 7.22% accuracy
captions: The baseline had severe errors on particular nights, including one night predicted entirely as wakefulness.
Four diagnostic rounds found no confirmed pairing, timing, channel or label-alignment defect.
scenes.note: Archived test results informed this diagnosis. Later R1 selection was post-hoc.

scenes.title: R1 changes the normalization rule
scenes.lead:
Each night supplies
its own mean and scale
body: Mean and standard deviation per frequency bin
The same rule applies to train, validation and test.
Unlabeled signals from the evaluated night supply statistics.
captions: R1 standardizes every frequency bin using the retained epochs of that same night.
R1 is post-hoc and transductive. Retraining plus normalization prevents a model-only causal claim.
scenes.note: R1 uses retained epochs whose selection includes hypnogram-based trimming. Waves are illustrative.

scenes.title: Archived results improved with R1
body: Pooled accuracy: 65.00% to 80.99%
The architecture and model seed remain fixed.
R1 is not an independent confirmation.
captions: Subject-mean macro-F1 rose from 56.42% to 74.86%. Pooled accuracy rose from 65.00% to 80.99%.
The comparison combines changed normalization with retrained weights and access to unlabeled test-night signals.
scenes.note: Historical test results. R1 and full-night sensitivity use offline, transductive normalization.

scenes.title: Sensitivity uses the complete PSG signal
body: Full-night statistics use all complete 30-second PSG epochs.
Training and evaluation epochs remain unchanged.
Subject-mean MF1: 71.84%. Accuracy: 79.10%.
captions: The sensitivity run computes statistics across the complete signal without labels selecting the normalization range.
It scores 71.84% macro-F1. It still uses each evaluation night's unlabeled signal and remains transductive.
scenes.note: Report R1 and full-night sensitivity together. Do not choose the better result as a new winner.

chapters.title: What the evidence does and does not show

scenes.title: The difference from R1 remains uncertain
body: Paired 95% CI: -7.12 to +1.22 points
The interval includes zero.
No sufficient evidence of a difference, not proof of equivalence.
captions: A paired participant-level bootstrap uses 1,000 resamples with fixed seed 20261011.
The run misses the 71.86% interpretation threshold by only 0.024 points. That threshold was not blind to R1.
scenes.note: Thresholds preceded this run but followed baseline and R1 results. CI omits model-selection uncertainty.

scenes.title: Results vary across held-out folds
body: All ten pooled fold macro-F1 scores increased under R1.
R1 folds 0 and 9 remain relatively weak.
Fold macro-F1 and subject-mean MF1 are different averages.
captions: A headline average hides fold variability. R1 improves fold macro-F1 in all ten paired folds.
These plotted values pool the two test participants within each fold. They are not the headline subject mean.
scenes.note: Saved fold results only. Training sets overlap across folds, so folds are not independent samples.

scenes.title: N1 remains the hardest class
scenes.lead:
R1 recalls 44.69%
of true N1 epochs
body: Other R1 class recalls range from 76.85% to 88.57%.
Full-night N1 recall is 39.51%.
Better overall performance does not solve every class.
captions: Per-class recall shows how many true epochs of each class the model recovers.
N1 remains the weakest class in both normalization runs, despite the overall improvement.
scenes.note: Pooled recall from archived test confusion matrices. Bar values are percentages.

scenes.title: Where R1's N1 errors go
body: 722 true N1 epochs become N2.
443 become W, and 376 become REM.
Rows are true labels. Columns are predictions.
captions: The confusion matrix separates correct classifications from the direction of each error.
N1 errors spread across adjacent or competing stages. This describes mistakes, not their biological cause.
scenes.note: R1 pooled confusion counts. Cell intensity uses within-row percentages, not raw counts.

chapters.title: Rejected pilots and the next evidence gate

scenes.title: Small validation pilots did not pass
scenes.lead:
No candidate met
the locked gain gate
body: Logit adjustment: +0.14 MF1 points
Head-only retraining: -0.52 points
Sequence decoder: -0.04 points
captions: Three bounded validation-only pilots tested class balance, the classifier head and transition decoding.
None reached the required one-point macro-F1 gain with the other safeguards. We kept the original settings.
scenes.note: Validation deltas only, not new test gains. Head-only comparison uses its matched FP32 baseline.

scenes.title: Independent confirmation is not ready
body: 30 have documented development exposure.
48 have unresolved prior-use metadata.
Unresolved history does not mean unused data.
captions: A provenance audit separates known development exposure from participants with unresolved histories.
No participant cohort currently meets the evidence requirement for a certified independent evaluation.
scenes.note: Metadata-only audit. Availability is not proof of independence.

scenes.title: Limits on the scientific claim
body: The complete pre-R1 attempt count is unknown.
Bootstrap intervals understate total uncertainty.
Historical source-hash and environment limitations remain.
captions: R1 uses a single model seed and was selected after baseline test failures. Its confidence interval is conditional.
These results do not establish clinical validity, equivalence to another paper, or online performance.
scenes.note: Subject-wise protocol differs from the paper; test < 10 subjects per fold (20 total)

scenes.title: A useful result with a clear evidence boundary
scenes.lead:
R1 scored higher
in this evaluated cohort
body: Base MF1 56.42%. R1 74.86%. Full-night 71.84%.
N1 and independent confirmation remain unresolved.
No further experiment is part of this presentation.
captions: The R1 package scored higher in this cohort. Normalization and retrained weights changed together.
The next scientific gate is a locked protocol and genuinely independent participants, after human approval.
scenes.note: Sleep-EDF Expanded 1.0.0. Kemp et al. 2000. Goldberger et al. 2000. ODC-By 1.0.
